description:
About the Position

The University of Amsterdam invites applications for a PhD candidate in access, actors and accountability, studying the role of researchers in AI governance. The project examines how knowledge produced by researchers enters AI governance processes, which actors gain access to regulatory arenas, and how accountability arrangements shape whose expertise counts when AI systems are governed.

The candidate will combine document and policy analysis with empirical research, including interviews and observational work in governance settings. The position is embedded in the university's interdisciplinary research on AI and society, and is a salaried four-year PhD track under the CAO-NU collective agreement with a gross monthly salary between EUR 3,204 and EUR 4,051.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a research master's degree in social sciences, law, philosophy, science-and-technology studies or a related field. Strong qualitative-research skills and analytical writing in English are expected, together with a demonstrated interest in AI governance debates.

Highlights

  • Role of researchers in AI governance
  • Access and participation in regulatory arenas
  • Accountability arrangements for AI systems
  • Policy analysis plus interview-based empirical work
  • Interdisciplinary AI-and-society research environment
  • Salaried PhD, EUR 3,204 - 4,051 per month (CAO-NU scale)

About University of Amsterdam

The University of Amsterdam (UvA) is the largest university in the Netherlands and one of Europe's leading research institutions. Its seven faculties span the humanities, social and behavioural sciences, economics and business, law, science, medicine in cooperation with Amsterdam UMC, and dentistry. PhD candidates at the UvA are employed on salaried contracts under the CAO-NU collective agreement, making doctoral research here fully funded. Academic vacancies and doctoral positions are published on the university's academic careers portal with detailed role profiles and application requirements.
